tasks.short: Coordinate utility information with engineers and field personnel

steps.what: Read the actual clearance status, switching-order references and distribution-change information
Coordinate the actual status information and practical constraints with engineers, planners and field personnel
Write the actual coordination-log entry with clarified status and unresolved issues
Save the coordination entry in the same operating-log system

tasks.design: Configure equipment-linked clearance and switching-order reference views in {OTHER}, the utility dispatch and operating-log system, with controlled references in {DOCS}. Keep actual coordination and the factual coordination-log write with the dispatcher.
tasks.previous_blocker: The dispatcher could have to locate related status records separately before coordination.
tasks.enabler_now: Native equipment and order links can narrow reference retrieval without issuing a clearance.
tasks.still_hard: Personnel need a shared understanding of live status and practical constraints.
tasks.human_edge: The dispatcher resolves ambiguity across the control room and field personnel.

ambition.what: No new clearance or switching authority.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: linked utility records can shorten status retrieval while live coordination remains human.

assumptions: This is actual coordination of existing clearance and order information, including the actual coordination log, not creation or issue of a new operative clearance. A real clearance issue or written order send needs its own exact-action authority and separate action.
Existing clearance and order records come from their actual authorized producers; s1 counts dispatcher identity, status and version checks. No free structured interpretation is assumed.
Test native dispatch links first; existing lookup capability earns no new saving. No additional meeting report is invented: s3 is the actual operating coordination record.
Same-system save1 is near-zero, fully retained and ungated. Shares are unmeasured estimates, independent of the supplied time prior.
unknowns: Current links between clearance and switching records
research_questions: Which actual repeated searches disappear with the native linked view?

already_counted.description: Status checks, actual personnel coordination and working-log writing remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain reference links and inspect stale versions.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R98 gives gross2 less upkeep0.5, net1.5. Low: clearance records lack stable equipment links, retaining19.5 of20 lookup hours;0.5 saved covers0.5 upkeep, net0. Conversation and actual coordination-log writing remain fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Read the actual distribution conditions and applicable equipment operating procedure
Determine the exact instruction, receiving operator and equipment operation needed
Check current system readiness and authorize the exact operating instruction under dispatch authority
Give the exact authorized operating instruction to the actual control-room operator
Verify the actual receiving operator's readback and reported status
Write the actual instruction and confirmed status in the operating record
Save the working instruction record in the same system

tasks.design: Link equipment references from {DOCS} into {OTHER}, the utility dispatch system. The dispatcher keeps the actual instruction decision, current readiness check, spoken direction, readback verification and post-instruction record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Applicable equipment references could require a separate search.
tasks.enabler_now: Native equipment and procedure-version links can shorten retrieval without issuing commands.
tasks.still_hard: Operating instructions depend on live system conditions and unambiguous readback.
tasks.human_edge: The dispatcher exercises actual operating authority and coordinates with the receiving operator.

ambition.what: No autonomous equipment command or expanded dispatch authority.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: linked procedure retrieval can support human dispatch preparation while operating commands remain under real human authority.

assumptions: Boundary includes the dispatcher's actual direction and working record. Receiving personnel's equipment operation remains their real work and is not claimed as dispatcher saving.
The dispatcher checks equipment and procedure identity in s1. The exact intended instruction exists in s2 before s3 current-condition authorization.
a1 is a real operational readiness gate on a spoken equipment command, not author approval of paperwork. Any instruction, recipient, equipment or current-condition change voids it.
Test native links first. Existing lookup and equipment runtime earn zero new saving. No machine command is proposed.
Actual completion entries follow verified status. Same-system save1 is near-zero fully retained and ungated. Shares are unmeasured activity estimates.
unknowns: Actual dispatch authority and readback procedure
research_questions: Does the native link avoid a repeated reference search without obscuring current status?

already_counted.description: Reference verification, instruction judgment, operational readiness, actual spoken direction and working-record writing remain counted.

approvals.approved_version: Exact instruction, receiving operator and equipment selected in s2 under current conditions checked in s3; any change voids authorization.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R98.5 gives gross1.5 less upkeep0.5, net1. Low: an equipment-specific revision lacks usable metadata, retaining14.5 of15 retrieval hours;0.5 saved covers0.5 upkeep, net0. Actual command, readiness, readback and record writing remain fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare switching orders to isolate work areas

steps.what: Read the actual power-system drawings, equipment status and work-area isolation requirements
Determine and capture the actual isolation sequence and continuity constraints
Assemble selected equipment tags and ordered actions in the working switching-order template
Write the actual order conditions, isolation explanations and cautions
Check the complete working order against current drawings and isolation and supply-continuity requirements
Save the working switching order in the same document store

tasks.design: Populate a working {DOCS} switching-order template with the dispatcher's exact selected sequence and equipment identifiers from {OTHER}, the dispatch drawing and equipment system. The dispatcher retains isolation design, wording and full drawing-based checking; the helper neither chooses switching nor issues an operative order.
tasks.previous_blocker: An already determined sequence and tag list were copied into the working order.
tasks.enabler_now: Native templates can assemble fixed selected fields without reasoning about network topology.
tasks.still_hard: A changed topology can invalidate an isolation and affect supply elsewhere.
tasks.human_edge: The dispatcher reasons about actual isolation and continuity under current system conditions.

ambition.what: No new switching or order-release authority.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: selected tags and an explicit human-designed action sequence can populate a working order template without automating switching decisions.

assumptions: Boundary is preparation of the complete working switching order, as stated. Actual operative issue, clearance grant, send or equipment switching requires its real final-version authority and separate action; none is hidden in a save.

The dispatcher reads current drawings in s1 and captures equipment identifier, selected action, sequence position, drawing version and isolation scope in s2. No free validated topology or machine-designed isolation is assumed.
Test existing switching templates first. Already generated order fields earn zero new saving; only actual repeated assembly is eligible.
Author checking remains content work, not author approval of a save. Save1 is near-zero fully retained and ungated. Shares are unmeasured episode estimates.
unknowns: Compatibility of drawing tags and order fields
research_questions: Can every populated action preserve the exact human-selected sequence and drawing version?

already_counted.description: Drawing review, isolation design, wording and complete working-order checks remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain tag mappings and switching-order template checks.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R85 gives gross15 less upkeep3, net12. Low: legacy drawing tags and template fields do not align, leaving10 of15 assembly hours manual;5 saved less3 upkeep gives2. Actual isolation decisions, caution writing and complete checks remain fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Monitor and record distribution control-board readings

steps.what: Identify the actual equipment, applicable operating context and readings to monitor
Monitor actual control-board readings and assess whether distribution equipment is operating properly
Transfer identified control-board values into the draft operating record
Write actual operating context and exceptions beside the readings
Check all recorded readings for equipment identity, time, units and actual operating meaning
Save the ordinary reading record in the same log system

tasks.design: Configure exact reading transfer from {OTHER}, the control-board historian, into its operating-log draft. Keep actual monitoring, exception interpretation and complete-record checking with the dispatcher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Some readings were copied from control-board displays into a separate operating record.
tasks.enabler_now: Native historian field mapping can reuse exact equipment, time and unit values.
tasks.still_hard: Reliable interpretation depends on instrument condition and actual distribution context.
tasks.human_edge: The dispatcher determines whether equipment operation is proper and responds to uncertainty.

ambition.what: No autonomous switching or monitoring decision authority.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: exact historian values can populate an operating record while live monitoring and contextual checking remain human.

assumptions: Boundary explicitly includes both monitoring and the actual reading record. Actual equipment control is separate and is not claimed as automation.

The dispatcher identifies tags, time basis and units in s1; actual readings are produced by existing instruments and observed in s2. Missing manual readings remain manual and no new free capture is assumed.
Test native historian-to-log configuration first. Existing automatic recording and native sensor runtime earn zero new labour saving.
The actual context write and whole-record check remain distinct from observation. Same-system save1 is near-zero fully retained and ungated. Shares are unmeasured activity estimates.
unknowns: Manual instrument and unit metadata gaps
research_questions: Which fields are actually recopied after current native log configuration?

already_counted.description: Context identification, live monitoring, actual narrative and complete-record checking remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain historian field mappings and inspect unit/time exceptions.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R80 gives gross20 less upkeep3, net17. Low: older instruments lack stable tag and unit metadata, leaving14 of20 transfer hours manual;6 saved less3 upkeep gives3. Live monitoring, context writing and whole-record checking remain fully retained.

role.altitude: Live distribution judgment and operating authority stay with dispatchers; selected lookup and record assembly consume less time.
reach: Work with the control-system engineer on tag and drawing-version mapping; learn historian provenance and template validation.
skills_to_grow: Clear separation of working orders and operative issue
role.ambitious_version: A dispatcher who maintains traceable working records while keeping equipment commands and isolation decisions under actual human operating authority.
